name: Microphthalmia-Motor Delay-Language Delay-Brain Anomalies-Diaphragmatic Hernia Syndrome
aliases: Microphthalmia with developmental delays and diaphragmatic hernia
Congenital microphthalmia with neurological and diaphragmatic defects

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Microphthalmia-Motor Delay-Language Delay-Brain Anomalies-Diaphragmatic Hernia Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of congenital microphthalmia confirmed by ophthalmologic examination or imaging
Developmental motor delay and language delay documented by clinical assessment
Neuroimaging evidence of brain structural anomalies such as corpus callosum hypoplasia or ventriculomegaly
Congenital diaphragmatic hernia confirmed by imaging or surgical findings
Additional features such as feeding difficulties, hypotonia, or seizures

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all four major criteria: congenital microphthalmia, motor and language developmental delay, brain structural anomalies, and congenital diaphragmatic hernia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by neuroimaging and ophthalmologic evaluation; genetic testing may assist but is not definitive.

pathognomonic.notes: Unilateral or bilateral small eye(s) present at birth
Defect in diaphragm causing abdominal contents to herniate into thoracic cavity
Includes corpus callosum hypoplasia, ventriculomegaly, or other malformations

common.symptomName: Global developmental delay including motor delay
common.notes: Delayed milestones in gross and fine motor skills
Delayed onset and progression of expressive and receptive language
Reduced muscle tone noted in infancy

searchTerms: problems with sucking or swallowing in infancy

common.notes: Epileptic seizures reported in some cases

occasional.notes: Head circumference below normal for age
Due to diaphragmatic hernia or pulmonary hypoplasia
Partial underdevelopment of corpus callosum on MRI
searchTerms: thin or small brain connection structure

rare.notes: Including septal defects or valve anomalies
Hearing impairment due to inner ear anomalies
Structural kidney abnormalities detected on imaging

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific biochemical markers identified
imaging: Brain MRI showing corpus callosum hypoplasia, ventriculomegaly, or other anomalies
Chest X-ray or CT confirming congenital diaphragmatic hernia
Ocular ultrasound or MRI confirming microphthalmia
other: Clinical developmental assessments documenting motor and language delays

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of diaphragmatic hernia and ocular anomalies

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress at birth due to diaphragmatic hernia
Marked developmental delays in motor and language milestones
Presence of brain malformations on neuroimaging
